article_title: Using Gemini and LuaLaTeX to transcribe physics videos into PDF/UA-2 and ISO 32005 math-accessible PDFs
citation: Looney, C. W., & Duston, C. L. (2026). Using Gemini and LuaLaTeX to transcribe physics videos into PDF/UA-2 and ISO 32005 math-accessible PDFs.
title: v6m AI video-transcription workflow (Gemini AI Studio + LuaLaTeX SE tagging + PDFix validation)
description: A mostly automated workflow that transcribes instructional physics videos with substantial mathematical content into math-accessible PDFs using freely available tools. Gemini in AI Studio listens to and watches the uploaded or linked video, sampling one frame per second, and produces LaTeX output under the v6m system instructions; the output is pasted into a prewritten LuaLaTeX preamble shell with automated Structure Element tagging and compiled locally, then validated with PDFix Desktop Lite for PDF/UA-2 and ISO 32005 compliance. The authors state it is "a free, widely available, mostly automated system that can make integrated use of the audio and visual information in a video".
requirements: A local-machine LaTeX installation with a modern TeX distribution compatible with 2026-standard math-SE tagging, since free web-based Overleaf times out on LuaLaTeX SE-tagged compilation
Users must strictly avoid inputting protected, sensitive, or proprietary institutional information into the free AI Studio tier
constraints: Tested primarily on introductory physics videos up to 20 minutes in length produced by two faculty members
No special instructions for English units are provided
target_learners: blind and low-vision students in undergraduate physics and mathematically intensive STEM courses
target_learning_goals: screen-reader-accessible reconstruction of spoken equations and visual arguments from instructional videos
examples: Sixteen test videos spanning lightboard, whiteboard, and screencast formats were transcribed; LaTeX sources and compiled PDFs are released in supplementary folders a-latex-files-v6m and b-pdf-files-v6m
